newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical wage talks adjourned to June 2.
newsitem.headline: German chemical wage talks adjourned to June 2.

text.p: Talks aimed at allowing employers in the German chemical industry to tailor wage levels according to company performance were adjourned until June 2, union and employer sources said late on Monday.

Hans Terbrack, chief negotiator for the IG Chemie trade union, spoke of progress in the latest round of talks in Frankfurt, saying that employers were now ready to discuss a union-proposed "income corridor" within which wages could be determined.

Employer negotiators had been seeking separate wage pacts for workers in the plastics processing, chemical fibres and rubber processing sectors, which they say have been hit hard by weak economic conditions.
But IG Chemie has been unwilling to agree separate wage accords for specific sector branches and wants its income model to apply across the whole industry.
Under the plan, companies would be able to pay wages at the lower end of the "corridor" in times of economic hardship, while offering staff bonuses during times of an upswing.
The union is demanding, however, that any such accords be coupled to job creation and protection measures.
